proposal:
# Re-rank note 2026-10-30 (10): the record-order fix (219) is released by the product owner's waiver and lands right after the fresh-probe seat gate (208)

- Led by: the product manager seat (fresh context, pm-rerank-10; Claude because the probes at 18:54 UTC (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota). Boundary: after the fresh-probe seat gate's (208) criterion 2 (a Claude seat starts only while no other model has quota, with the reason in the record). To be decided by objection window 208-rerank-10 (D153); every declared role is polled (architect, QA engineer, backend developer, independent reviewer (audit lens), delivery lead, product manager (signoff)); D158 checklist to be written as .mob/records/208/checklist-208-rerank-10.md. Proposal, trail and decision commits are added by the facilitator when the window closes.
- Trigger: product owner ruling D162 waives the stop-the-line gate for the record-order fix (219) only, and asks for a re-rank at the next boundary with true priority order restored. Number order is no longer forced once 219 lands, so this note re-ranks on value and dependency; it moves only what that fact changes.
- Before (note 9): 208, 210, 211, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 219, 217, 218, 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207.
- After: the fresh-probe seat gate (208, finishing its criterion 3, the pinned probe model), the record-order fix (219), the record checker hardening (210), the MD-010 fix (211), the loop's corrective-card gate (220), the loop running a card in its own repository (221), the loop's retro and re-rank steps that stop on failure (222), the per-card retro from every role (223), the re-rank by the product manager and a Decider (224), card mode reading only role lines (225), then the acceptance-suite flakes (217), the mid-card retro removal (218), and 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207 unchanged.
- Next card: after criterion 2, the fresh-probe seat gate (208) continues with its criterion 3 (pinned probe model); the first card after the fresh-probe seat gate is the record-order fix (219).
- Rationale (one line): the record-order fix (219) moves from tenth to second, right after the fresh-probe seat gate (208) closes, because it is the one card whose absence makes every later corrective close out of number order refusable (the held record for 209 and the lock-down loop cards), while the rest keep their order since the record checker hardening (210) is the only lock-down rule that binds the hand-run cards today and the loop's corrective-card gate (220) alone does not yet make the loop usable.

## Why 219 after the fresh-probe seat gate (208), not before its criterion 3

- Criterion 3 (the probe model is pinned per backend in core/backends.json) is independent of 219 and of criterion 2, and is the smallest increment of 208 (about 70 lines, 3 files). Nothing waits on 219 until the first close out of number order, and that cannot happen before 208 itself closes.
- 208 closes in number order today, so its record is not refused by the checker; pausing 208 after criterion 2 would leave two cards open at once (the paused 213 shows the cost) and put 208's close behind a card that touches the same checker for no gain.
- Finishing 208 closes MD-002, one of the three failures that stop the line, before the waiver is used. D162's "normally right after the current criterion" is a default; the team's call is to take the boundary at the card end because the criterion is a one-increment finish. Reverse by moving 219 ahead of criterion 3 if the delivery lead reports that the 208 close is in danger of the record-order refusal.
- The waiver covers 219 only and ends when 219 closes (D162); 219 must land before 210 or any card that closes out of number order, including the held 209 record (blocker 2026-10-30-209-record-order) and 213's.

## Why the others stay

- The record checker hardening (210) stays ahead of the loop's corrective-card gate (220): every card is still hand-run, so the record checker and pre-push hook are the only enforcement that binds today; 210 reads the `quota_reason` field that 208 criterion 2 now writes, and it edits the same checker as 219, so doing them back to back avoids rework. The MD-010 fix (211) stays with it to close the third failure.
- The loop's corrective-card gate (220) does not move above 210: alone it lets the loop start a corrective card, but the loop still runs a card in the wrong repository until 221 and still ignores a failed retro or re-rank until 222, so the loop is not usable for lock-down cards before 222 either way. 220 to 222 stay together as the next block, so the runner becomes usable at the earliest point.
- Out-of-order closes inside 220 to 225 become safe once 219 is on main, which removes the delivery-lead blocker risk that note 9 listed.
- Product cards (213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207) and the cards 217 and 218 stay behind the lock-down (D161). 217 and 218 drop below 225 as before; nothing in this note ranks product work above process work.

## Known cost and risk

- The loop's corrective-card gate (220) is still arguably worth more than 210 and 211; if hand-running stops being the norm, move 220 first at the next boundary.
- 208 does not get the record-check rules 210 adds (D160 C5) until after it closes; unchanged.
- 219 starts while MD-003 and MD-010 are open, under the waiver (D162); the product owner owns that exception, and no gate code changes.
- The first test of the new order is whether 208's close, then 219's, then 210's land without a checker refusal; if one fails, the delivery lead raises a blocker.
